label: ligero-linear-test-structured
note: B-Ligero linear test q_add through the structure of r^T A (LINTEST.md): under the protocol's powers-of-rho combination and a unit-major constraint order, r^T A on a Ligero row is a per-row F_c scalar times one of M fixed rows (M = 3 for the chain layout: witness pattern, helper pattern, sum constraint) + ~130 exceptional rows (unit 0, last unit, table-side helpers, multiplicities). q = sum_m enc(E_m) * enc(sum_i s_im W_i): one fused pass over W (combine_multi, 6M accumulators) + 12M transforms per BATCH + F_c pointwise + the general path for the exceptional rows. Measured per B batch (310,602 rows): M=1 5.66 ms (0.89 of the 5.05 ms read floor), M=1 + 256 exceptional rows 6.37, M=2 + 256 7.03, M=4 + 256 13.67 ms (INT32-issue-bound from M >= 3) vs the general path 150.5 ms in the same run (14 transforms/row): 26x / 21x / 11x. Bit-exact vs the b-commit GPU path (Combiner.linear) and numpy; the toy chain-system test proves the structure exactly. Tensor-core variant of the pass (torch._int_mm, INT8 s-limbs x W bytes, exact recombination, bit-exact): 10.3 ms M=1 (0.49 of floor, 2.4% of INT8 peak), 12.4 M=2, 16.7 M=4, plus an 11 ms byte-xor pass unless the witness is stored xor'ed: SIMT wins at every M; the operation is a memory-bound GEMV and cuBLASLt's skinny INT8 kernel does not reach bandwidth. Same test, same transcript: prover-side algorithm change; conventions to fix: unit-major constraint enumeration, rows hold whole units.

label: B re-priced, structured linear test (4090)
note: Candidate B on the RTX 4090 with every bucket measured and the linear test STRUCTURED (b_measured_4090.md): 122.9 ms per 4096-VU batch = 30.0 us/VU, overhead 3.05e6 (was 258.7 ms / 6.41e6 with the general-path linear test; 2.1x). Buckets: fused Blake3 commitment 49.4, linear test 13.7 (M=4 + 256 exceptional rows, the conservative measured configuration; M=2 gives 7.0 ms and 116.3 ms / 2.88e6), IRS 5.7, quadratic 7.8, inversions 28.8, openings 5.1, modelled 12.5 (90% measured). The linear test fell from 58% to 11% of the batch; the commitment (encoder-bound, 0.39 of its SIMT floor) and the helper inversions (0.52 of traffic floor) are now B's buckets. Scalings (labelled, not measurements): H100 150.9 ms / 3.74e6, A100 276.5 ms / 6.86e6 by the INT32 issue-rate ratio; the structured linear test is memory-bound, so for that bucket bandwidth scaling (A100 x0.65, H100 x0.30 of the 4090 time) is the right rule and these scalings overstate it. No B bucket is a tensor-core operation: the one candidate matmul (the row combination) is a memory-bound GEMV where SIMT beats cuBLASLt INT8.
